children: Arkham has launched Tracer v2, an upgraded tool for following fund flows through bridges and across chains. Users can start from any address, map counterparties, and filter traces by token, value, time, or chain. The release was demonstrated on the Bybit and Drift exploits, showing how the tool traces stolen funds across multiple networks.

For ARKM, the upgrade is a product-utility change rather than a token-level event. Tracing tools are Arkham's core offering, and cross-chain coverage addresses a practical gap, since funds moved through bridges are harder to follow with single-chain views. If the tool draws more analysts and investigators to the platform, usage of Arkham's services could rise, which is the main channel through which this release relates to the token.

The impact stays bounded for now. Arkham has not stated adoption figures or revenue effects tied to Tracer v2, so the release is best read as a capability upgrade whose market relevance depends on subsequent usage.

We just finished building Tracer v2, Arkham's tool for following fund flows through bridges and across chains. Start from any address, pull its counterparties onto the network map, and follow the money hop by hop.

title: Arkham: Tracer v2 goes live for cross-chain fund-flow tracing - 22 Sep 2026
